_about: Quest Forge client profile. Read by tools/lite-client/apply-profile.ps1 on Windows and by the Mac's Prism tooling. Keys that start with _ are comments. Every setting is client-side video, HUD or audio: the server never sees any of it, so the world, mobs, items, recipes and quests are identical by construction. 'why' gives one line per setting: what it buys, and what it costs in looks. Section keys: options_txt (vanilla options.txt, key:value), angelica_options (merged into config/angelica-options.json), angelica_modules (config/angelica-modules.cfg, Forge B:/I:/S:/D: keys), shaders (config/shaders.properties + shaderpacks/<pack>.txt), optifine (the OptiFine E7 fallback client only), mods_aside (jar-name prefixes moved out of mods/), resourcepacks (packs selected in options.txt's resourcePacks list), jvm (Prism memory by installed RAM).
title: Potato: integrated graphics
hardware: Laptop or desktop on integrated graphics (Intel Iris Xe, Radeon Vega 8, Intel UHD 620 class), 4 cores, 8 GB shared RAM, 1280x720 or 1366x768

why.options_txt.renderDistance: 5 chunks: one less than the server sends. Fewer chunk sections to build on 4 cores and fewer to draw on an iGPU. Looks: the fog starts one chunk closer.
why.options_txt.fancyGraphics: Fast graphics: opaque leaves, no entity blob shadows, fast rain. Looks: solid leaf blocks.
why.options_txt.ao: Smooth lighting off, together with use_celeritas_smooth_lighting false: flat per-block light. Looks: visibly flatter walls and caves; this is the one potato change you will notice indoors.
why.options_txt.particles: Minimal: only the particles the game needs to show what happened. Looks: fights and rain lose most of their particles.
why.options_txt.mipmapLevels: 1 mip level: the animated-texture re-mip each tick is nearly free, and one level still tames most distant shimmer. 0 would cost texture cache hits on an iGPU and shimmer badly; 4 is the full cost.
why.options_txt.maxFps: Cap at 60: an iGPU shares the laptop's thermal budget with the CPU; running flat out throttles both. Nothing visible on a 60 Hz panel.
why.options_txt.enableVsync: Off; Angelica paces frames through vsync_mode.
why.options_txt.clouds: Clouds off with shaders off (one less draw, less overdraw). The QuestForge pack draws its own sky regardless. Looks: a clear sky.
why.options_txt.fboEnable: Framebuffer objects on; required by every shader loader.
why.options_txt.advancedOpengl: Vanilla occlusion queries off (Angelica culls on its own).
why.angelica_options.quality.biome_blend_rad: No biome colour blending: the cheapest chunk build. Looks: hard colour lines at biome borders.
why.angelica_options.quality.use_celeritas_s: Off, with ao 0: no corner shading. The cheapest chunk build and the flattest look.
why.angelica_options.quality.texture_filter_: NONE: plain bilinear plus mipmaps. An integrated GPU pays for every texture sample. Looks: distant floors blur and shimmer a little more.
why.angelica_options.advanced.vsync_mode: OFF: the maxFps cap paces frames without vsync's input lag.
why.angelica_options.performance: Celeritas's culling and deferral switches on (its defaults). No cost in looks.
why.angelica_options.reducer: Angelica's FPS reducer: 10 fps while another window has focus, 20 fps after 5 idle minutes, menus capped. Nothing changes while you play.
why.angelica_modules.B:enableDynamicLights: Dynamic lights off: no chunk re-renders around a held torch. Looks: a held torch lights nothing until you place it.
why.angelica_modules.I:droppedItemLimit: At most 128 dropped items drawn (Angelica's default is 256): an item explosion or a death pile stops costing a frame. Content: every item still exists and can be picked up.
why.angelica_modules.B:showSplashMemoryBar: Angelica's loading-screen memory bar off: it would draw over the Quest Forge mural.
why.shaders: The QuestForge pack at QF_PRESET 0 (Potato): the sky, water, auto-exposure and colour grading, with no shadow pass at all, no TAA (an FXAA-class filter instead) and no bloom. OpenGL 3.3 only. Budget: 6 ms of shader cost at 720p on Iris Xe / Vega 8 (docs/design/shaders/performance-rules.md). Below that class (Intel UHD 620 and older) run the same profile with shaders off: apply-profile.ps1 -Profile potato -Shaders off. if_missing 'off': no QuestForge pack installed means shaders off.
why.optifine: OptiFine E7 fallback client only. Lite's OptiFine settings plus: clouds off, no connected textures, no stars, no rain splash, water, portal or potion particles, no animated items, vanilla AO level 0.
why.mods_aside.SoundFilters: Cave reverb and muffling. Ray-traces block occlusion per sound. Content: none (the server has no such jar).
why.mods_aside.MobDismemberment: Gore entities on death. Content: none.
why.mods_aside.MobAmputation: Gore entities for player-like mobs. Content: none.
why.mods_aside.CustomMenu: Branded title-screen buttons; splash and music stay. Content: none.
why.mods_aside.journeymap: The minimap and the full-screen map (M). Its mapping threads re-render map tiles as chunks change and compete with the game for 4 cores. Content: none; you navigate by landmarks and coordinates (F3).
why.mods_aside.DamageIndicators: The targeted mob's health bar and portrait (it draws the mob a second time every frame) and the damage numbers. Content: none.
why.resourcepacks: QF Textures (resourcepacks/QFTextures.zip, decision 0006): vanilla designs with Faithful 32x detail, connected glass and panes, the modded ores on Faithful stone, LabPBR maps the QuestForge shader can read. Selected after the packs already chosen (the branding pack QuestForge.zip stays). The same in every profile: it costs texture memory, not frame time (measured within 0.02 ms of vanilla). if_missing 'keep': when the zip is not in the resourcepacks folder, the selection is left alone.
why.jvm: 3 GB on 8 GB: with integrated graphics the GPU's memory comes out of the same 8 GB, so the heap stays small. 3.5 GB with 12 GB, 4 GB with 16 GB or more.
